rationale: B best balances the visible requirements with clarity and manufacturability: it presents two coordinated faces, unmistakable Indian tricolor and Ashoka-wheel imagery, strong foundation naming, and a clean aviation/space motif that should translate well to a challenge coin. C is similarly complete and more illustrative, but its crowded stars, overlapping aircraft, and finer details reduce hierarchy and production reliability. D is bold and memorable with a clear tricolor, though low-contrast gold lettering and presentation of only one distinct face weaken it. E shows a coherent two-face metallic set but lacks an unmistakable Indian flag and loses legibility at small scale. A has credible embossed styling and a strong central motif, but appears least complete and does not clearly satisfy the visible flag/logo requirement.
uncertainty_notes: The excerpt omits exact size, material, finish, required wording, and reverse-side instructions. Low-resolution renders also make it difficult to judge fine lettering, relief depth, and whether some monochrome elements are intended to represent the flag.
